links.site_note: No campaign website; Ballotpedia lists only an email. A Wix page reported elsewhere was not opened.

oneliner.t: Perennial Green and alternative-party candidate (on the ballot in Arizona and Colorado since 2012) who won the 2026 Green nomination in AZ-06 as a write-in with 29 votes and says he is running a zero-dollar campaign.

hometown.t: Gloucester County, New Jersey area (Mullica Hill High School)

profile.residence_note: Not documented. He ran for Colorado state Senate in 2024; his current Arizona address was not found.

upbringing.t: Born in Willingboro, N.J., he attended Mullica Hill High School and delivered newspapers as a teen. He earned a bachelor's (University of Colorado Boulder, 1991; political science per his survey) and a graduate degree (University of Colorado Denver, 1999; MPA per his survey). He describes himself as a caregiver and neighborhood business-association promoter and a spokesperson for Best Democracy.

education.deg: Master of Public Administration (per his survey)

career.role: Caregiver; neighborhood business association promoter; spokesperson, Best Democracy

platform.t: Cut the U.S. military budget by at least 90%, close foreign bases, end foreign military aid and interventions, abolish nuclear weapons.
Proportional representation, abolish the U.S. Senate and Electoral College, national initiative and referendum.
Universal basic income, Medicare for All, carbon taxes, legal abortion; emphasizes ecological limits and a steady-state economy.
Impeach and convict Trump and his cabinet (Secretary of State candidate statement).

promises.t: Run on proportional representation and deep military-spending cuts.

record.t: FEC shows no financial summary data for his 2026 candidate ID; Ballotpedia shows $0 for his past races.

claims.claim: The Arizona Green Party's endorsed candidate for AZ-06.

record.t: Won the Green primary as a write-in (29 votes) and is the Green ballot nominee; the party's Aug. 31 'sham candidate' complaint named other nominees, not him.

claims.claim: Has appeared on the ballot 13 times as an alternative-party candidate since 1996.

record.t: Ballotpedia documents about nine general-election ballot appearances from 2012 to 2024 (plus write-ins and withdrawals); pre-2012 runs are not listed.

claims.claim: Won 138,634 votes in a U.S. Senate race in '1996.'

record.t: The vote total matches his 2016 Arizona Senate race against John McCain (5.5%); the year is wrong.

claims.claim: B.A. in political science and M.P.A. from the University of Colorado.

record.t: Only self-reported; no university record checked.

aipac_pac.note: career — not listed on Track AIPAC as of 2026-10-08

statements.t: Supports ending all U.S. foreign military aid (general position; no Israel-specific statement found).

fec.src_note: FEC shows no financial summary data for 2025–26 and no principal committee on the page (statement of candidacy filed July 19, 2025). Zeros reflect 'no reports', consistent with his zero-dollar statement.

history.office: Various (CO-1, CO-6, AZ Senate 2016, AZ-7 2018, CO-2 2020, CO SoS 2022, CO Senate 2024)
history.note: Ballotpedia lists $0 contributions where data exists; FEC pages for earlier candidate IDs (e.g., H8AZ08224) were not opened (rate-limited).

money_flags_note: No money reported in any cycle found; Track AIPAC lists nothing.

note.t: No House candidate disclosure found; candidates below the $5,000 threshold need not file.

groups.name: Green Party (Arizona; Jefferson County, Colo.); Unity Party of Colorado; Best Democracy (spokesperson)

debates.note: Not part of the Sept. 10 Clean Elections debate (only Ciscomani and Mendoza took part); whether he was invited is not stated.

note.t: Ran in Arizona (2016, 2018, 2025, 2026) and Colorado (2012–2014, 2020–2024); current residence not documented.

checks.legal: Not searched beyond general news searches on his candidacy (nothing found).
checks.claims: No campaign site. Sample = his July 2026 Arizona Daily Star column and his Ballotpedia survey bio claims. 5 rated: 2 true, 1 partly, 2 unverifiable.

research_notes: Thin record by design: a self-described zero-dollar candidate. The AZ ballot file listed two possible FEC IDs; H6AZ06164 is confirmed on fec.gov as SWING, GARY, Green, AZ-06 (2026). Ballotpedia's 2026 listing mentions independent Trevor Dickerson, who is not on the verified printed ballot. Photo not retrieved.
